summary: The paged kernel originally took `MAX_BLOCKS` (= block_tables width) as a `tl.constexpr` loop bound. Triton recompiles per distinct constexpr value, so under the mixed/long sweep (sequence lengths grow and vary widely) it recompiled for nearly every block-count — ~1 s each, holding the backend lock — which looked like a hang (worker stalls, requests pile to `pending` and time out, no traceback). Fixed by making the loop bound a **runtime** per-sequence `n_blocks` derived from `seq_len` (compiles once; also optimal — no padding-block iterations). Confirmed on GPU: block-counts 2→128 all 0.1–0.5 ms, no spikes. **Lasting rule:** never put a value that varies with input shape/length in a Triton `constexpr` — only genuinely-fixed things (head_dim, block_size).
title: Triton constexpr on a data-varying value → recompile storm
